title: Dead fish found along Yamuna near Burari, industrial pollution flagged - The New Indian Express
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Several dead fish were spotted along the Yamuna near Burari in north Delhi on Wednesday morning, raising concerns over water quality and possible industrial pollution.
Residents of nearby Islamnagar Colony and Eidgah Colony collected fish found along the riverbank. Wildlife experts and environmental activists flagged untreated industrial effluents and low dissolved oxygen levels as possible causes, though the exact reason remains unconfirmed.
Bhim Singh Rawat, a Yamuna activist and member of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP), said mass fish deaths are usually reported in summer when high temperatures reduce oxygen levels in water.
Calling the latest incident unusual after the monsoon, Rawat warned that recurring fish mortality in the relatively cleaner stretch upstream of Wazirabad threatened the river’s remaining aquatic biodiversity.
He said restricted environmental flows and untreated effluents entering drains from Haryana could be contributing to the problem. He cited reports of industrial waste entering Drain No. 2 in Panipat and earlier fish deaths in the Baghpat stretch of the Yamuna.
Rawat called for stricter pollution control and adequate environmental flows, questioning the effectiveness of multi-crore river-cleaning efforts by the Delhi and Haryana governments. The incident has also raised concerns ahead of Chhath, when thousands of devotees are expected to visit the river. Contact with polluted water could pose health risks to those entering it.
In a post on X on Thursday, the New Delhi Nature Society said hundreds, possibly thousands, of fish were found dead near Burari on October 14. The group said the cause remained unknown, while locals alleged that chemical waste was being discharged from Haryana through canals. It also questioned whether the deaths could be linked to acid rain reported on October 12.
In May, hundreds of fish died at Sanjay Lake in east Delhi amid a heatwave and receding water levels, renewing concerns over aquatic life in the capital’s water bodies.

title: Dead fish found along Yamuna banks in Burari - The Tribune
full_text:
Thousands of dead fish were found along the banks of the Yamuna near Burari in North Delhi on Wednesday, raising fresh concerns over the river’s water quality and aquatic ecosystem.
The New Delhi Nature Society shared photographs and videos of the incident on X on Thursday, showing dead fish along the riverbank. The organisation said the specific cause of the deaths had not been established.
“Locals allege that the deaths might be linked to chemical waste discharged from Haryana through canals,” the society said in its post, clarifying that the allegation had not been confirmed.
According to the society, mass fish deaths can indicate ecological stress, including deteriorating water quality, low levels of dissolved oxygen and the presence of toxic substances. The cause of the deaths, however, remains unclear.
The incident comes amid continued concerns over pollution in the Yamuna, which has faced persistent challenges despite repeated efforts to clean the river.
A similar incident was reported near Burari in May last year, when visuals showed thousands of dead fish floating in the river. At the time, locals had attributed the deaths to chemical waste allegedly discharged from Haryana, while reports pointed to high pollution levels.
In May this year, hundreds of fish also died at Sanjay Lake in East Delhi amid a heatwave and falling water levels. Experts had cited high temperatures, concentrated pollutants and declining dissolved oxygen levels as possible contributing factors.
The latest incident has once again drawn attention to the vulnerability of aquatic life in Delhi’s water bodies. However, no official findings establishing the cause of the fish deaths were available at the time of filing this report.
